public_claim: Study A contains 192 accepted formal observations balanced across four surfaces and two rounds.
scope: Eligibility and evidence QA do not make the sample representative of all users, geographies, accounts, or time periods.
approved_wording: In this frozen desktop study, 192 formal observations passed evidence QA.

public_claim: Visible task-criterion coverage averaged 98.3% for ChatGPT, 95.1% for Google AI Mode, 65.7% for TikTok, and 47.5% for YouTube.
scope: Search surfaces were scored from titles/captions/metadata, while agent surfaces used complete initial answers. Coverage is lexical/task-criterion alignment, not factual correctness.
approved_wording: The agent answer boundaries covered more of the frozen task criteria than the visible search-result boundaries in this design.

public_claim: Google AI Mode generated all 24 Round 1 answers but only 16 of 24 Round 2 answers; eight Round 2 observations preserved fallback web results plus an explicit generation error.
scope: One account/browser/time window cannot estimate a platform-wide failure rate; fallback results remained visible and sometimes relevant.
approved_wording: Generation reliability varied sharply across the two captured rounds.

public_claim: Exact outputs changed across rounds even when task coverage was comparatively stable; median round overlap was platform-specific and never implied deterministic reproduction.
scope: Search surfaces use URL overlap; agent surfaces use answer-token overlap. The measures are not interchangeable quality scores.
approved_wording: Role-level behavior was more stable than exact output identity.

public_claim: Constraint coverage and provenance legibility were separate capabilities: agent answers organized constraints, while search surfaces preserved direct creator/channel origins and item URLs.
scope: Visible origin does not establish authority; a synthesized source label does not guarantee a durable accessible URL.
approved_wording: The strongest product opportunity is to connect intent, claims, and original evidence rather than replace every surface.

public_claim: Across 136 checks in six named validation tasks, three claims were coded incorrect; all three were narrow robot-vacuum overclaims in captured Google AI Mode answers.
scope: The truth set is narrow, product-specific, and single-coded; 37 checks were not addressed and 36 were ambiguous or unsupported.
approved_wording: The named validation set exposed three incorrect claims that a verification queue should catch.

public_claim: In the strict survey layer (n=73), 30 (41.1%) preferred approval before cross-tool carryover, 26 (35.6%) preferred automatic carryover, and 17 (23.3%) preferred no carryover.
scope: Anonymous convenience sample; retrospective choices, not observed behavior. Expanded layer n=122 is sensitivity only.
confidence: Moderate as an exploratory product signal
approved_wording: The sample split across three consent preferences, so handoff control should be explicit and user-selectable.

public_claim: Direct links or citations was the most selected improvement in both layers: 25/72 (34.7%) strict and 39/121 (32.2%) expanded.
scope: Respondents could choose up to three improvements; one over-limit response was excluded from this item only.
approved_wording: Direct evidence access was the clearest recurring improvement signal in this sample.

public_claim: Results are reported as surface-specific task-fit roles because the evidence families use different captured boundaries.
scope: Post-hoc three-family profiles are provided only as sensitivity checks and do not replace the preregistered four-family composite.
approved_wording: The evidence supports a task-fit role map across four captured surfaces.
